title: Locally constant maps form a sheaf of sets
statement: Let U be a topological space and R a set. A map from an open subset V of U to R is locally constant if every point of V has an open neighbourhood in V on which the map is constant. For each open V let L_R(V) be the set of such maps, with restriction maps. Then L_R is a sheaf of sets on the site of open subsets of U with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: compatible locally constant maps on an open cover glue uniquely to a locally constant map.
